title: The Second Supplement — 2 is a Quadratic Residue mod p iff p ≡ ±1 (mod 8)

problemStatement.plain: The parent entry proves Euler's criterion: a nonzero residue $a$ is a perfect square modulo an odd prime $p$ exactly when $a^{(p-1)/2} \equiv 1 \pmod p$. That criterion is universal but it does not by itself tell you, for a *specific* number $a$, which primes $p$ make $a$ a square. This leaf carries out that computation for the smallest interesting case, $a = 2$: it asks to prove the classical "second supplementary law" of quadratic reciprocity, namely that $2$ is a square mod $p$ precisely when $p$ leaves remainder $1$ or $7$ when divided by $8$ (and is a non-residue when the remainder is $3$ or $5$). For example $2$ is a square mod $7$ ($4^2 = 16 \equiv 2$) and mod $17$, but not mod $5$ or mod $11$.
